comment: Assemblies whose full member surface is stored in every baseline. Keep this to assemblies a Revit-side project actually redistributes: indexing everything Revit ships costs about 5 MB per version for libraries no add-in would ever carry. RefCheck emits RVTREF004 when the build references a Revit-shipped assembly that is missing here, so gaps report themselves - add the name, re-collect, commit. See readme.md for why each entry is on the list.
deniedComment: Simple names a Revit-side build must not ship, in any version. This is NOT a surface comparison: the failure happens one level below, when a name is bound to a file, and a matching surface does not prevent it. Measured twice - System.Memory on Revit 2024 and Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration on Revit 2026, where the add-in did not load at all. A name may appear here and in assemblies at the same time; the two lists answer different questions and this one wins. A trailing * matches a prefix. The BCL polyfills a net48 build legitimately carries - System.Buffers, System.Memory, System.Numerics.Vectors, System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe - are deliberately absent.
